To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the more students are involved with service-learning, the more they become engaged in civic life, and the more they become committed to civic participation; (b) the more students engage in service-learning, the better their critical thinking and writing skills; (c) the more students become involved with service-learning the more likely they are to be involved in other types of out-of-class learning activities; (d) service-learning is a pedagogical tool that works well in a variety of disciplines

(1) the more students engage in service learning, the higher their academic performance and the greater their civic engagement; (2) students who engage in service learning have higher levels of self-esteem, are better adjusted to school, are more likely to graduate from high school, and are less likely to engage in delinquent behavior; and (3) service learning has a positive effect on students' social skills and attitudes.

(1) service-learning is an effective pedagogical approach to teaching civic engagement, but only when it is well designed and implemented; and (2) service-learning can be a powerful tool to promote the civic engagement of students, but only when the service-learning experience is well designed and well implemented.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how students and teachers experience and make sense of the service-learning process and how these processes affect the development of civic and democratic values, skills, and behaviors.
the question of whether service learning is a pedagogical approach that is likely to enhance student learning and development.
the question of how to design and evaluate service learning programs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Service-Learning is a teaching method in which students learn and develop through thought and action.
the work of citizenship, and the problem of service-learning, is the problem of public work.

the service-learning movement is a response to the crisis in civic education, a response that seeks to reengage students in the civic life of their communities, to make them more responsible citizens, and to reinvigorate democratic life and public institutions in a society that seems increasingly apathetic and alienated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an understanding of the role of the teacher and the student as active agents in the process of learning.
we are interested in the relationship of citizenship and service, and the role of the service-learning experience in that relationship.
service learning is an effective way to promote civic education and community development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
service learning is not just a pedagogy.
service learning has the potential to transform students' lives and the communities in which they live.
service learning can and should be a vehicle for the development of citizenship, but it will be a vehicle only if the work of service-learning is understood as a form of work.
